meta.title: NOSTALGIA Map v2 - terrain (hills, rock fields, elevation)
meta.format: [lat, lon] WGS84; heights in metres above sea level (asl) and relative to the surrounding ground (rel_height_m = summit minus the 15th-percentile ground 0.7-1.5 km around)
meta.for_the_game: suggested: map rel_height_m to world height with the 3D vertical scale (VS); the city floor is ~500-540 m asl (Musi valley ~490-505, Banjara/Jubilee ridge ~590-635, HITEC plateau ~590-630)

confidence_rules.high: summit position/height from data and identity from data or several sources
confidence_rules.medium: from data but identity by position, or extent derived from a DEM threshold

attribution: Map reference: DataMeet Municipal Spatial Data (CC BY 4.0) and (c) OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL)
Elevation: Terrain Tiles on AWS Open Data (Mapzen/Tilezen joerd, Terrarium encoding), derived from SRTM (NASA, public domain)
Peaks, cliffs and bare rock: (c) OpenStreetMap contributors (ODbL) via Overture Maps Foundation
caveats: DEM is ~30 m source data resampled to ~9 m pixels: summit heights +-10 m, outlines are generalised; buildings/trees are not in SRTM bare-earth everywhere (urban canopy can add a few metres).
Rock-field polygons mark the high rocky ground from the DEM, not individual boulders; boulder density is a game-art decision (Banjara/Jubilee and HITEC were far rockier in 2003 than today).

hills.name: Naubat Pahad / Kala Pahad (Birla Mandir hill)
hills.outline_rule: DEM contour at 529 m (base + 35% of relief) around the summit
hills.source: elevation: Terrain Tiles (Terrarium, zoom 14, ~9 m pixels, SRTM-based, public domain NASA data; AWS Open Data elevation-tiles-prod / Tilezen joerd); name/identity: OpenStreetMap (ODbL) via Overture base/land
hills.note: twin-summit rock hill: Birla Mandir (1976, white marble) on the north summit, Birla Planetarium (1985) on its west flank; the OSM peak node "Naubat Pahad" marks the south summit

rock_fields.name: Banjara Hills - Jubilee Hills granite boulder fields
rock_fields.rule: DEM ground >= 588 m inside box lat 17.4-17.447, lon 78.395-78.452 (largest patches >= 4 ha)
rock_fields.source: elevation: Terrain Tiles (Terrarium, zoom 14, ~9 m pixels, SRTM-based, public domain NASA data; AWS Open Data elevation-tiles-prod / Tilezen joerd); rockiness: general knowledge of the Deccan granite terrain + OSM bare_rock/peak features
rock_fields.note: Deccan granite tors and boulder piles on the ridge between Panjagutta, Jubilee Hills Check Post and Film Nagar; in 2003 many plots between the mansions were still bare rock
